newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf states to raise tobacco tariffs to 70 pct.
newsitem.headline: Gulf states to raise tobacco tariffs to 70 pct.

text.p: Gulf Arab states have agreed to raise customs duties on tobacco to 70 percent from the current 50 percent, Gulf newspapers on Sunday quoted an official statement as saying.

The statement by the secretariat of the Gulf Cooperation Council -- which groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates -- said the duties would be reviewed upwards again in the year 2000.
The statement did not say when the rise would take effect, but GCC officials had at a summit meeting in Qatar earlier this month said it would be from July 1997.

The summit said the six states needed another two or three years to unify all customs tariffs, a key condition by other major trading groups for forging a free-trade accord with the oil-rich alliance.

European Union and GCC talks on a free-trade deal have been blocked for more than 10 years by the EU's demand that GCC states should first unify tariffs. Standard tariffs range between four to 12 percent in the six states.
